instruction: Add bold formatting to all italicized words in the document so they become bold italic.

command: import pyautogui; import time; pyautogui.hotkey('ctrl', 's'); time.sleep(0.5);

metadata.trajectory_summary: Agent successfully used Find & Replace with formatting to change all italic text from 12pt to 14pt in LibreOffice Writer document. Used the Replace with Formatting dialog to target italic style and set replacement size to 14.
metadata.capability_extraction: Can use Find & Replace with formatting options in LibreOffice Writer, can selectively modify font properties of styled text, can navigate formatting dialogs
metadata.task_rationale: Tests same Find & Replace workflow but adds bold to italic text instead of changing size. The agent proved it can target italic text via formatting search, so applying a different formatting attribute is a natural variation.
metadata.explanation: Task requires adding bold formatting to all italic runs. Getter checks bold status of each italic run. Metric returns proportion of italic runs that are also bold (partial credit). [Fixed: corrected MD5 hash suffix from truncated 8-char to full 32-char hash. Fixed: removed old function definitions from deprecated files with truncated hash.]

scoring_breakdown.italic_bold_match: proportional - fraction of italic runs that also have bold formatting

fix_history: Fix 1: Corrected MD5 hash suffix from truncated '1e896fa7' (8 chars) to full 32-char hash '7532d291294fb4f3bb8e25015109f986' computed from 'e246f6d8-78d7-44ac-b668-fcf47946cb50|1'. Updated getter function name, metric function name, evaluator references, and file paths.

Fix 2: Removed old function definitions from deprecated files (check_italic_bold__1e896fa7.py, docx_italic_bold__1e896fa7.py) that had invalid truncated MD5 hash suffixes. Files now contain only deprecation comments.

llm_judge_reasons: Getter correctly identifies italic runs and checks their bold status, matching the instruction requirement.
Metric computes proportion of italic runs that are also bold, providing appropriate partial credit scoring.
Postconfig correctly saves the file (Ctrl+S) before getter reads it, ensuring fresh state.
Coverage is complete: the single instruction requirement (all italic text should become bold italic) is fully verified.

Minor concern: python-docx run.italic returns None (falsy) for italic formatting inherited from paragraph styles rather than explicit run-level italic. This could cause the getter to miss some italic text, leading to an incomplete check. For most typical documents this is unlikely to be an issue.
llm_judge_fix_suggestions: Consider using run.italic is not False (or checking the resolved font.italic property) instead of just 'if run.italic:' to also catch italic formatting inherited from paragraph styles.
